[b]February 23, 2028: the deal with Pirn[/b]

Whereas: The nation of Pirn is a stable and good state
Whereas: It sits in a location of strategic importance and is in dire need of reserves and relations
1. The government of Rosenmarkke shall provide an annual of 1.4% of its gold reserves to the government of Pirn for the increase of their defensive and infrastructure needs.
2. The government of Rosenmarkke shall permit the presence of Pirn based companies and goods within Rosenmarkke.
3. The government of Rosenmarkke shall provide military data and cooperation to the Pirn armed forces.
4. The government of Pirn shall maintain 10% or less tariffs on all Rosenmarkket goods.
5. The government of Pirn shall be permitted free trade and corporate cooperation with the government and people of Rosenmarkke, with 5% or less Tariffs placed upon all goods from the Pirn by Thýven.
6. Access to the White Strait shall be unencumbered by the government of Rosenmarkke, and no fee of travel shall be placed upon ships originating from Pirn by Rosenmarkket port authorities, save that for Tharkønn which shall place no more than a 2% fee on the total value of all goods onboard any ship from Pirn.
7. A comprehensive security agreements shall be drawn up for the sharing of data and cooperative training to be signed on this or a later date.

[b]February 23, 2028: A Sobering Reality[/b]

In a preliminary meeting with the board of directors of the national bank, along with members of the National Budget Council, Polenne Strømm was warned regarding continuing the hostile anti-EDU stance, with advisors stating that the EDU held massive economic projection powers over Elseyr and isolating Rosenmarkke from those networks was detrimental overall to the stability of the state. With the further warning that investors had begun to leave the nation for other economically safer options. 

The NBC would further warn that if inflows and economic growth didnt outpace spending the government would be forced to enact mass austerity measures and cuts to crucial programs, forcing another SCSID intervention into the state.

Furthering the issue independent economic watchdogs in Rosenmarkke would release a joint paper slamming the optimistic outlook of the NBC in their initial January report and citing that the economy under the NDP was for all intents and purposes on the verge of a recession due to the irregular transitions that the NDP had mandated. 

In a statement which denied the independent economic reports released by the offices of the triumvirate Strømm would be cited as saying: Economic victory is at hand, these tremblings are merely a part of a process towards permanent growth,

[table=plain][tr][td]🅸n what could prove to be a defining year in Banhock politics, the nation is finally geared up for another traditional half-decade political cycle's initiation, a pivotal period in the nation's flavorful and historic philosophical culture. While there was hope that this year it'd be different, Banhockia is, possibly momentarily, returning to its binary partisan system for this term, as it seems extremely unlikely that the rising third party, Union 45, will be victorious in this year's plebiscite. Following their presidential candidate's withdrawal from the race mere days from the printing of ballots (though this doesn't mean the party won't stand for any kind of office), it seems like it will be the typical battle, the one Banhocks have known since the inception of the republic's political identity. The verticists, represented by the ruling [b]CGT[/b], and the horizonists, faithful to [b]Advance, Banhockia![/b] with some independents also running on their own agendas.

The general overview of the contest makes it seem rather unceremonious in its happening; the typical competition between the same two forces that will result in a slight difference in the nation's governance over the next few years. Despite voter sentiment signalling such, it is important to note that this will be an election that could test that understanding of national politics for a while. It has been endlessly covered how 2028 will find whether people see that the path that had previously been selected, with AB! in charge, is more viable than the concurrent one which is being led by the controversial CGT. Even if the reelection of AB! might mean a return to the ideals envisioned by former president Emmelei Gehurlae, it would also be radically changed by the fact that the party now knows that it is far from invincible, after the disastrous 2023 election which brought it to where it currently stands, at a meek 12 seats in the Junior Directory.

Additionally, in the new age of internationalism, Banhockia seeks to adapt itself in a way that will benefit on its own while also assuring its long-lasting security, both militarily and economically. Large movements in this aspect haven't been achieved in a while, the most impactful one remembered being entering [url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2743488][b]PECA[/b][/url] over 20 years ago, a choice which, according to some polls, was 'unnecessary' to most Banhocks. Though, things have changed since then, given the diffusion of online services, an occurence which Banhockia can attest to as its own internet providers have extended their influence worldwide, and the globalizing market which Banhockia, with vast unused lands and opportunities for projects such as green energy and manufacturing, may find advantageous. This debate has existed for a long time but truly came into question in the last few years, as AB!'s grip on power loosened and the CGT proposed to limit foreign interference and ensure that Banhock territory would remain in its own citizen's hands. It seems as though that this, excluding the new deterioration of the order set in the last few decades, will be the most important topic in this election.[/td][/tr][/table]
